_source: Jagatjit Agri Engineering Limited DRHP dated 25-Sep-2026 (SEBI filing 01-Oct-2026). Rs crore = Rs million / 10. Printed page numbers (PDF page - 6). Restated: FY26 consolidated, FY25 and FY24 standalone (the businesses of Saron Mechanical Works I and II came in from 1-Apr-2025; the DRHP gives pro forma FY25/FY24 for comparison, pp. 90-92).

basis.name: Jagatjit Agri Engineering Limited
basis.outside: BRLM owner and Amir Chand price: secondary sources, unverified (see merchant_bankers.json)

1.finding: 22:1 bonus (27-May-2026) and 2:1 split are applied to EPS and NAV for all years: FY26 EPS Rs 5.64 = Rs 313.90 m / 5,56,50,984 shares.

2.finding: FY26 CFO Rs 26.85 m against PAT Rs 313.90 m (8.6%). Inventory +Rs 445.46 m and other assets +Rs 281.35 m absorbed the cash; receivables released Rs 242.66 m. Cumulative FY24-26 CFO Rs 281.93 m against PAT Rs 404.39 m (69.7%); FY24-25 CFO is standalone and was funded by payables to the promoters' proprietorships (Rs 160.70 m and Rs 259.02 m payables increase).

3.finding: Current tax Rs 130.30 m on PBT Rs 444.12 m (29.3%); cash tax paid Rs 104.52 m (p. 88). Profit is taxed in cash.

4.finding: Promoter advances outstanding Rs 45.00 m (Jagatjit Singh) and Rs 10.00 m (Dharam Singh); the Dehlon plant (16.20 acres) is leased from Jagatjit Singh at Rs 0.08 m a month and Rs 716.64 m of proceeds expand it. FY24-25 standalone purchases from the two proprietorships were Rs 420 m / Rs 256 m of Rs 735.68 m / Rs 462.13 m cost of materials.

5.finding: Fresh issue is amount-based (Rs 3,000 m); share count undisclosed, so no objects price floor. Specific objects Rs 2,001.64 m; the rest is offer expenses and GCP (cap 25% of gross).

7.finding: Goodwill Rs 4.55 m (0.6% of net worth) from the Jagatjit Energies acquisition.

8.finding: Top customer 25.21% and top-10 50.04% of FY26 revenue (top-5 40.84%); top-3 products 64.40%; Northern states 68.04% and Central 25.95%. Top-10 suppliers 40.53% of raw material cost, no long-term supply agreements.

9.finding: Contingent liabilities Rs 29.35 m plus bank guarantees Rs 42.35 m = 10.1% of net worth; GST demands Rs 22.67 m. Materiality threshold Rs 6.74 m (p. 488).

R1.finding: Promoters Jagatjit Singh and Dharam Singh were appointed directors on 29-Sep-2020 while disqualified (to 31-Oct-2021) over Jaggatjit Agro Pvt Ltd; adjudication application filed 11-Sep-2026, pending. The issuer attributes it to conflicting MCA records. Not a current disqualification.

R2.finding: Audit trail at database level was not enabled in the accounting software until January 2026.

R5.finding: Offer is under Reg 6(2): the issuer fails Reg 6(1)(a) and (c) (net tangible assets and net worth tests), so at least 75% must go to QIBs or the offer fails.

R6.finding: Keynote track record compiled from the DRHP: two issues in FY27 to date.

R7.finding: Rs 1,100 m (36.7% of gross) funds working capital and Rs 185 m repays debt; a monitoring agency is named (p. 11).

rationale.g1: FY26 revenue Rs 4,139.70 m is +63.1% on the pro forma FY25 Rs 2,537.60 m (+22.3% pro forma FY25 on FY24) (p. 92). Industry: farm equipment Rs 1,397 bn FY26, 7.7% CAGR to FY30 (issuer-paid CARE report, p. 205). Capacity is 73.6% (Cheema) and 89.7% (Dehlon) used (p. 267) and the Dehlon expansion is funded from FY28 (p. 124), so FY27 is capacity-bound. Bear: demand flat to subsidy-driven; Neutral: 15% then 18% as capacity arrives; Bull: super-seeder share gains.
rationale.m: EBITDA margin 13.46% FY26, 14.51% pro forma FY25, 9.74% pro forma FY24 (p. 158). Neutral uses the three-year average 12.57%; Bear the FY24 level; Bull the FY25 level. Gross margin rose from 23.58% to 39.06% once the proprietorships were absorbed (p. 158).
rationale.nwc: Issuer working-capital table (standalone, p. 126): Rs 1,029.46 m FY26, Rs 658.57 m pro forma FY25, Rs 402.36 m pro forma FY24 = 24.9% / 26.0% / 19.4% of revenue. Neutral uses the three-year average 23.4%; management projects inventory 130 days, receivables 45 days (p. 127).
rationale.roic: Issuer RoCE 31.10% FY26, 31.55% pro forma FY25 (p. 158). Neutral terminal ROIC 18% is above the WACC of about 14.4%; Bear 13% stresses a return to commodity-implement margins.
rationale.g2: Neutral 18% reflects the Dehlon expansion funded in FY28 (p. 124) adding capacity after FY27 is capacity-bound (p. 267); Bear 8% without IPO funding; Bull 30% with share gains (p. 246).
rationale.g3: Industry projected at 7.7% CAGR FY26-30 (issuer-paid CARE report, p. 205); Neutral 15% is about twice that while the new capacity fills.
rationale.g4: Growth fades towards the industry rate as the base grows; Neutral 12%, Bear 6%, Bull 20%.
rationale.g5: Year 5 Neutral 10% against a 7.7% industry CAGR (p. 205); terminal growth 4.50%.
